question: A finance shared-service team already has a working month-end checklist and wants to bring Claude into it without disrupting the close. What should they do first?
options: A) Pick one checklist step that is text-heavy and repetitive and try Claude there
B) Ask Claude to rewrite the whole checklist before the next month-end close runs
C) Replace the checklist with an arrangement built around what Claude can do now
D) Have every preparer use Claude however they prefer during the next close cycle
correct_answers: A) Pick one checklist step that is text-heavy and repetitive and try Claude there
explanations: Correct. Augmenting a process that already works means starting with the smallest, most suitable slice, where a failure is contained and the rest of the close carries on unchanged.
Rewriting the checklist before anyone has tried a single step changes the whole close on an untested assumption.
Redesigning around the tool is the wrong move when the existing process works; it puts a hard deadline at risk for no demonstrated gain.
Uncoordinated individual use during a deadline-driven close produces inconsistent output and no learning the team can reuse.
